2014_072_111114mtg.paragraph: Troy School District's Board of Education assembled this packet for its regular meeting of November 11, 2014, held at 7:00 PM in the Services Building, 4420 Livernois, Troy, Michigan. Most of the packet is financial attachment: the July, August and September 2014 Treasurer's Reports, each with a Pentamation check register, wire transfer and ACH/P-Card listings, and fund-by-fund budget reports, showing total disbursements in period of $6,741,175.21, $7,318,697.46 and $7,167,418.80 respectively. The board's most consequential action item was the appointment of Rick West as Assistant Superintendent of Business Services on a two-year probationary administrative contract without tenure, effective December 1, 2014, filling the post vacated by Mark Rajter.

**Meeting**
Troy School District Board of Education, regular meeting, November 11, 2014, 7:00 PM, Services Building, 4420 Livernois, Troy, Michigan 48098; district offices at 4400 Livernois, 248.823.4000. Meetings are cablecast on TS-TV Channel 19 (Comcast) and Channel 15 (WOW) Mondays and Wednesdays at 2:00 and 9:00 p.m., and streamed at http://vimeo.com/troyschools.

**Recognitions**
Lisa Carruthers, third-grade teacher at Leonard Elementary, for bringing "Peer to Peer Mediation" — an evidence-based practice supporting students with Autism Spectrum Disorders — into her classroom. Tracey Kinney, TSD Assessment Coordinator, for the NUMATS (Northwestern University's Midwest Academic Talent Search) Outstanding Educator Award; in 2014 only 18 educators in the United States were singled out.

**Consent agenda**
Minutes of the October 7, 2014 regular meeting, the October 21, 2014 workshop, and the October 21, 2014 special meeting; Treasurer's Reports for July, August and September 2014.

**Budget reports, Fiscal Year 2015**
The General Fund (funds 101, 120, 122) carries an approved revenue budget of $131,253,100 and an expenditure budget of $132,525,180, excess revenue over (under) expenditures of (1,272,080), and fund balance printed as 21,380,015 opening and 20,107,935 closing on all three monthly statements. September YTD actual revenue is 18,427,658 against actual expenditures of 19,042,182 with 6,330,317 encumbered. Other funds' printed balances: Consolidated Special Revenue 3,541,661 to 4,336,763; Food Service (520) 1,320,716 to 1,758,788; Troy Career Center (529) 1,973,956, unchanged; Adult & Community Education (530) 0 to 357,030; Facilities Rental (535) 246,989; Debt Service (306, 307, 312, 314) 853,935 to 523,230; Capital Projects Maintenance (499) 803,719; Internal Service (681) 25,318. Debt Service budgets property taxes of 15,456,298, principal redemption of 10,600,000 and interest of 5,843,818.

**October actions recorded in the minutes**
Resolutions 14-102 through 14-110, all adopted 7-0 except 14-107. Highlights: sixty-seven National Merit and one National Achievement scholarship semifinalists honored; resignations of Kenneth Miller (Executive Director of Maintenance and Operations) and Mark Rajter accepted; food-service wireless temperature monitoring awarded to SMART Temp, LLC for $38,504.00 (6-1, Schmidt opposed); Athens High School masonry awarded to Efficient Design, Inc. for $73,482.00; Superintendent Richard Machesky named temporary Treasurer. The October 21 special meeting gave Rob Carson a two-year probationary contract as Director of Maintenance & Operations effective October 27, 2014.

**Personnel considerations, November 11**
Stacey Palmer, probationary contract, 3rd grade, Troy Union Elementary. Rick West, Assistant Superintendent of Business Services, two-year probationary administrative contract without tenure, effective December 1, 2014. Jan Keeling, Assistant Superintendent of Elementary Instruction, resignation for retirement effective January 1, 2015; date of hire November 15, 1977.

**Business**
Annual Summer Tax Resolution: continue summer collection of one-half of school property taxes, including debt service, beginning with 2015, pursuant to 1976 P.A. 451, as amended; collection expenses negotiable under MCLA 380.1612; notice to the City of Troy to be received before January 1, 2015; adoption certified under the Open Meetings Act (Act 267, P.A. 1976).

**Other**
Bond projects update by a Barton Malow representative, and Dr. Machesky's report on his 90-day entry plan. Both reports; no action required.
2014_072_111114mtg.verbose:
**Meeting identity.** Regular meeting of the Troy School District Board of Education, November 11, 2014, 7:00 PM, Services Building, 4420 Livernois, Troy, Michigan 48098. District address 4400 Livernois, phone 248.823.4000, www.troy.k12.mi.us. Board meetings are cablecast on TS-TV Channel 19 (Comcast) and Channel 15 (WOW) every Monday and Wednesday at 2:00 and 9:00 p.m. and viewable at http://vimeo.com/troyschools. The meeting fell a week later than usual because of the November 4 elections.

**Recognitions.** Lisa Carruthers, a third-grade teacher at Leonard Elementary School, was to receive a certificate for implementing "Peer to Peer Mediation," described as an evidence-based practice that positively affects students with Autism Spectrum Disorders. Tracey Kinney, TSD Assessment Coordinator, was presented a certificate for the NUMATS (Northwestern University's Midwest Academic Talent Search) Outstanding Educator Award; in 2014 only 18 educators from the United States received this recognition.

**Minutes of October 7, 2014.** President Dr. Philippart called the meeting to order at 7:00 p.m. with Edmunds, Fleming, Hauff, Miletti, Schmidt and Underwood present, plus Superintendent Machesky, administrators Birmingham, Dziatczak, Keeling, Mull, Whan and Witt, four high school student representatives (Dalia Ibrahim of Athens, Alexandra Levin and Avirath Kumar of International Academy-East, Sylvester Hanna of Niles, Patty Durell and Bobby Hahn of Troy High) and approximately 75 audience members. Resolution 14-102 honored one National Achievement Scholarship semifinalist, Noah McNeal, and sixty-seven National Merit Scholarship semifinalists; nationally, more than 160,000 students entered the National Achievement program and only 1,600 became semifinalists, while more than one million students from some 22,000 high schools entered the National Merit program and 16,000 became semifinalists, scoring in the top one and one-half percent on the PSAT (Yes 7, No 0). Resolution 14-103 approved the September 2 minutes, the September 16 workshop minutes and the June 2014 Treasurer's Report (7-0). Resolution 14-104 accepted the resignations of Kenneth Miller, Executive Director of Maintenance and Operations, and Mark Rajter, Assistant Superintendent of Business Services (7-0). Resolution 14-105 approved new hires Meredith Adkins, Taylor Firman, Rebecca Johnson and Holly White (7-0). Resolution 14-106 seated the 2014-2015 Sex Education Advisory Board, co-chaired by Amy Buchanan and Nicole Jenkins, with teachers Lisa Danhoff, Karen Wakely and Kevin Wilson, Rev. David Huseltine of Big Beaver United Methodist Church, and nurse Lois Winer of the Oakland Health Department (7-0). Resolution 14-107 awarded the food services wireless temperature monitoring system equipment and installation bid to SMART Temp, LLC for $38,504.00 as an expenditure of the 2014-2015 Food Services Fund, carrying 6-1 with Schmidt opposed. Resolution 14-108 appointed Superintendent Dr. Richard Machesky temporary Treasurer of the Board until an Assistant Superintendent of Business Services is appointed (7-0). Resolution 14-109 awarded masonry work for the Athens High School addition and remodeling project to Efficient Design, Inc. for $73,482.00 from the 2014 Capital Projects Fund (7-0). Resolution 14-110 adopted the 2014/2015 board committee assignments (7-0). The meeting adjourned at 9:58 p.m.; Karl Schmidt signed as Secretary. Reports covered the 2013-2014 teacher and administrator evaluation summary (Jasen Witt), professional development (Anne Mull), and Advanced Placement results (Mark Dziatczak), in which TSD students exceeded both the state and national average AP pass rate by more than 20%. A new Superintendent's Student Advisory Board drew 55 applications and seated 24 students — 6 seniors, 7 juniors, 7 sophomores and 4 freshmen — with a first meeting on October 22. Wattles and Bemis were congratulated for National Blue Ribbon awards, and Doug Madden of Barton Malow flagged a possible delay to the Troy High auditorium because seats might not arrive on time.

**October 21, 2014 workshop and special meeting.** The workshop ran 6:00 p.m. to 9:10 p.m. on food service equipment purchases and the Superintendent's 90-day entry plan. The special meeting, 9:15 p.m. to 9:23 p.m., issued Rob Carson a two-year probationary administrative contract without tenure as Director of Maintenance & Operations effective October 27, 2014 (7-0).

**Disbursement detail.** The Pentamation ACCTPA21 "Check Register — By Fund" runs for accounting periods 2/15, 3/15 and 4/15 (check dates 07/01–07/31, 08/01–08/31 and 09/01–09/30/2014), all on cash account A1003 with zero sales tax. Wire transfer listings include MPSERS UAAL Rate Stabilization payments of 312,111.99 and 312,455.34, Sodexo food service settlements, and MILAF-to-Bank of America transfers for bond payments.

**Personnel items.** Item 6.A: a probationary contract for the remainder of 2014-2015 to Stacey Palmer, 3rd grade, Troy Union Elementary — B.A. in Sociology from Michigan State University, May 1998; Michigan Provisional Certificate April 2013; long-term guest teacher through Temporary School Staff, Dearborn, April 2013 to October 2014; student teaching in Troy, January 2011 to April 2012; Troy resident. Item 6.B: Rick West appointed Assistant Superintendent of Business Services on a two-year probationary administrative contract without tenure, effective December 1, 2014, coming from Royal Oak Schools where he spent three years as Executive Director of Finance and Operations after four years as Business Manager for Atherton Community Schools; he is President of the Oakland County School Business Officials, holds an MBA from Texas A&M and a BBA from the University of Michigan–Flint. Item 6.C: Jan Keeling, Assistant Superintendent of Elementary Instruction, resigning for retirement effective January 1, 2015; hired November 15, 1977; formerly principal of Bemis and Morse Elementary Schools, a PACE teacher, and a classroom teacher at Schroeder Elementary.

**Business — Annual Summer Tax Resolution.** Item 8.A asks the Board to continue summer tax collections for the 2015-2016 fiscal year and to notify the City of Troy. The attached resolution recites that the Board, by resolution of November 11, 2014, determined to impose a summer property tax levy collecting one-half of school property taxes, including debt service, beginning with 2015 and continuing year to year until revoked, pursuant to 1976 P.A. 451, as amended. The Superintendent or designee is directed to forward the resolution to each city's governing body for receipt before January 1, 2015, and is authorized to negotiate the reasonable collection expenses a city may bill under MCLA 380.1612, with any agreement returned to the Board. Conflicting resolutions are rescinded, and the Secretary certifies adoption at a regular meeting noticed under the Open Meetings Act (Act 267, P.A. 1976, as amended).

**Other reports.** Item 10.A, a bond projects update by a representative of Barton Malow, and item 10.B, Dr. Machesky's summary of the outcome of his 90-day entry plan as superintendent; both are reports requiring no action.
